text:
Alex Laferriere is doing almost everything the Kings ask except watch the puck go in. He has 5 goals on 9.7 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a 7.2% shooting rate against a league norm of 13.4%, and Los Angeles has scored 5.4 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. We flag him as due.

The role is the good news. He's playing 19:41 a night, up from 18:19, and he's on the ice for 74% of the Kings' power-play chances after 30% last season. His own chances are up to 1.34 expected goals per 60 from 0.96, and at five on five Los Angeles takes 55.8% of the expected goals with him on, 9.3 points better than without him. He has added 70 hits in 22 games.

The finish may be turning. He has scored in two of his last three, a power-play goal against Anthony Stolarz in Toronto on Nov. 19 and another in Montreal on Monday. For a third-round pick out of Harvard, the job is already won; our numbers say the shooting percentage is the part most likely to move next.
